systems.owner: Ministry of Education and Technical Education (MOETE)
systems.tiers: not stated; named only in 'EMIS data', one of the feeds of the Education Decision Support System stage that this restructuring drops; the paper does not say what EMIS does or who enters its data

systems.country_label: Smart Card; Student Digital Identity; Smart Student digital ID
systems.tiers: as of February 2024 a pilot due to conclude by June 2024; target redefined to all grades 4-11 students in one governorate (data for grades 1-3 'mostly compiled' but no cards printed); to hold per student health and biometrics, special needs, schools attended, teachers, grade 9 and 12 scores, receipt of tablets and books, for use by authorised levels of administration; who enters the data is not stated

systems.country_label: Education Decision Support System; Education Decision Support Dashboard
systems.tiers: stage 2 (training, assessment and EMIS data, with staff training at ministry, directorate, district and school level) dropped; stage 1 recast as the Digital Content Dashboard

systems.owner: MOETE, Central Administration for Technological Development
systems.tiers: to be developed by December 2024; real-time usage data on grades 4-12 digital learning content by grade, gender, user type and school location, with quarterly reports to each level of administration

systems.system: Egyptian Knowledge Bank, Learning Management System and TV educational channels
systems.country_label: EKB; LMS; study.EKB; Madrastena; Edmodo; YouTube livestreaming
systems.tiers: grades 4-12 students and teachers; open access with no login required

systems.country_label: assessment management platform; tablet-based assessment management and delivery platform
systems.tiers: item bank, administration and marking of grades 10-12 tests; results available to students, teachers, school principals and district officers

note: No fact: the paper names EMIS only as a data feed and never says schools enter per-learner records into it or into the smart card, so neither is classed. Its one dated statement on the card: as of February 2024 MOETE was piloting it, to conclude by June 2024, in one governorate, financed under a US$500 million IBRD loan.
